cards.explanation: The answer is to love and serve Him with all your heart. Moses says the LORD asks Israel to fear Him by walking in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve Him “…with all your heart and with all your soul…” Notice he doesn't say "serve Him when it's convenient." I've stamped cookies with a tired mustache before, friends, and showing up and meaning it are two different batches.

The answer is good. Moses says the commandments and statutes are given "…for your own good?" So he's not handing Israel a pile of rules to trip over. Think of a recipe card, friends: the steps feel like a lot until the cookies come out right.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD set His affection on Israel's fathers and loved them, and that He has chosen their descendants “…above all the peoples, even to this day.” Here's the part I love, friends: the heavens and the earth are His, so He had every choice there was. And He still set His affection on them.

The answer is hearts. Moses says, "Circumcise your hearts, therefore, and stiffen your necks no more." I think he's pointing at something deeper than the outside. When the preacher says hearts, friends, you know he isn't talking about your hat.

The answer is False. Moses says the LORD “…executes justice for the fatherless and widow…” Leaving them to fend for themselves isn't what he describes. He says it right after telling Israel the LORD shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.

The answer is True. Moses says the LORD “…loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.” That love shows up as real provision, friends, not just a nice feeling. Then Moses turns it around: Israel must love the foreigner too, since they themselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

The answer is that they were foreigners in Egypt. Moses says, “So you also must love the foreigner, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.” That's the reason he gives them. I think anyone who's been the new person in a room knows what he's getting at.

The answer is False. Moses says the fathers went down to Egypt seventy in all, and now the LORD has made Israel "…as numerous as the stars in the sky." From a small group to a sky full. I know a little something about stars, friends, and I'm still counting on them to show up.

The answer is waters. Moses says the LORD "…made the waters of the Red Sea engulf them as they pursued you…" The Egyptian army, horses and chariots included, was chasing Israel when it happened. Moses wants them to remember it, friends, because their own eyes saw it.

The answer is that the earth swallowed them. Moses says it happened in the midst of all the Israelites, when "…the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them…" Dathan and Abiram were sons of Eliab the Reubenite. Moses says it to remind everyone what they saw with their own eyes.

The answer is False. Moses says the earth opened its mouth and swallowed Dathan and Abiram, “…their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.” So it wasn't just the two men, friends. Their households and tents went with them.

The answer is strength. Moses says keeping every commandment is “…so that you may have the strength to go in and possess the land…” Israel is about to cross the Jordan, and strength is the word he gives for going in. I've tried hauling a full cookie rack on pure confidence, friends, and confidence doesn't lift a thing.

The answer is that it drinks the rain from heaven. Moses says the land across the Jordan is "…a land of mountains and valleys that drinks in the rain from heaven." That's the contrast with Egypt, friends, where they irrigated on foot. Here the water comes down from above.

The answer is False. Moses says it's a land for which the LORD cares, and His eyes are always on it "…from the beginning to the end of the year." So it isn't only harvest time, friends. Every day of the year counts.

The answer is grass in the fields. The promise is, “…I will provide grass in the fields for your livestock…” and Moses adds that they will eat and be satisfied. So both the animals and the people are fed. A full table is a good sign, friends.

The answer is that He will shut them. Moses says if Israel turns aside to other gods, "He will shut the heavens so that there will be no rain…" Then the land won't yield its produce, and they will soon perish from the good land. It's a serious warning, friends, and he says it straight.

The answer is morning and night, at home and away. Moses says to speak about them “…when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.” That covers at home and away, and from waking to bedtime. It isn't a once-a-week thing, friends, it's a way of living.

The answer is True. Moses says, "Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates…" So the words are right where you come and go. It's hard to miss a message, friends, when you walk past it twice a day.

The answer is True. Moses says if they keep these commands, "…the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you." Greater and stronger than Israel, friends, and still the LORD drives them out. The size of the other side isn't the deciding thing.
The answer is False. Moses says, "No man will be able to stand against you…" Not a few, friends, not any. The LORD will put the fear and dread of Israel on all the land, as He has promised.

The answer is curse. Moses sets two outcomes in front of Israel: a blessing for obeying the LORD's commandments, and a curse for disobeying them. The curse is tied to turning aside and following other gods they have not known. He doesn't blur it, friends, and he doesn't leave them guessing which road leads where.

The answer is Mount Gerizim. Gerizim is the mountain for the blessing, and Ebal is the one for the curse. Moses even adds directions: across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, near the Oak of Moreh. Directions with a landmark tree in them are my kind of map, friends, though I'd still manage to get lost.
